title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a seed never stores a roll-up (summary) value; the children compute it, and the load says what it dropped
body:
Fixes #35655

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: follow-up #36122

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：应用作者在演示数据或安装包自带的数据里给父记录写的汇总数（如发票的「已收金额」）不再被存下，汇总数一律由明细算出；只写了汇总数、没带明细的父记录现在显示 0，启动日志会点名是哪个对象、哪些字段、丢了几个值。
- 为什么做：按你选的 D「一律不存汇总数」；过去写进去的数时对时错，重启后还会把真实合计盖回去，明细也可能因为写的合计被应用自己的规则拒掉。
- 出错会怎样：受影响的只有在演示数据里写了汇总数的应用作者，他们会看到数字变成明细合计或 0，并在日志里看到提示；不改任何已存数据，撤回本次改动即恢复旧行为。
- 要你做什么：这次改动让演示数据和安装包里原来能存下的汇总数改为不存（收紧），按规则需要你本人批准后才能合并。

## What changes

A seed never stores a value a seed record supplies for a roll-up (`summary`) field, on insert or on update. This follows maintainer ruling D as analysed in 7062334196, with the seat's correction 7064615114. The roll-up is computed from the child rows. The drop is reported by one warn notice per dataset, which is the whole report: no load-result key is added. The change is in the loader only: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` is not touched.

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`
  - Module helper `summaryFieldNames(definition)` returns every field a definition declares `type: 'summary'`, whatever its aggregate and whether or not it is `readonly`. It keys on `type === 'summary'` literally, as the engine's roll-up readers do.
  - In `loadDataset`, the roll-up fields are the union of `summaryFieldNames` over the resolved definition AND over the engine's merged schema (`engine.getSchema`, read through the new private `engineSchemaOf`, which `resolveObjectDefinition` now shares). The metadata service's copy wins `resolveObjectDefinition` whenever it has `fields`, and that copy carries no object extension, so a roll-up an extension contributes is read from the engine's schema (contract review S1b). An engine without a schema registry, or whose read throws, leaves the resolved definition the only source.
  - Each such key is deleted right after the record's expressions resolve, before anything else reads the record. So the no-op replay compare, the insert and the update all see the record without it.
    - A created row starts the column at its empty-child-list value (the engine's existing `initializeSummaryFields`), and the child inserts compute it, as before.
    - A matched row keeps the value it already holds.
  - One `warn` per dataset names the object, the fields and how many values were dropped (`{ object, fields, droppedValues }`). A supplied `null` counts as a value. A dry run (`validate`) logs the same notice.
  - `success` and `errored` do not move. One row counter does: on a replay (`upsert` or `update`), a matched row whose only difference from the seed record was a roll-up value is now counted `skipped`, with nothing written. It used to be counted `updated`.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-summary-value-not-stored.ts`: the ADR-0087 semantic entry for the narrowing. No tombstone and no D2 conversion, because no key is added or removed and no rewrite is mechanical. It names the manual repair for a parent with no child rows that an earlier load stored a total on (review nit n3): insert a child row under it and delete that row again.
- `.changeset/35655-seed-summary-value-not-stored.md`: `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `minor`, with a BREAKING banner, `adr-0087: registered seed-summary-value-not-stored`, FROM → TO, the compatibility note for seed authors, and the same manual repair (n3).
- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`: the sentence "seed data, package installs and a historical import … keep a pre-computed total" is rewritten to the ruled behaviour. The historical import (`treatAsHistorical: true`) keeps its sentence, because it is a separate door. The degraded path is named (review S2): when the runtime has no metadata service, or the seed loader throws, it falls back to a basic insert of the seed records, and that fallback still stores a supplied summary value. Ruling D keeps the change loader-only.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` (review S1a): Rule 1's sentence no longer says seed data and package installs write a roll-up from a system context. It names the roll-up's own recompute and a historical import, and says the seed loader takes a seed record's value out before the write.
- Comment-only edits in objectql, to text this change made false:
  - the `summaryFieldsLockedOnWrite` docblock in `engine-top-level.ts`;
  - the `summary` note in `validation/rule-validator.ts`;
  - the header and one test name of `engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts`.

  They no longer say a seed load keeps a pre-computed total. The engine behaviour they describe (an `isSystem` write keeps its value) is unchanged, and so is the test's assertion.
- Stale test comments (review nit n1): `packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts` (the comment above, and the name of, the "system writer supplied on insert" case no longer list seed loads) and `packages/spec/src/data/field-autonumber-readonly.test.ts` (the `summary` note no longer says a caller may seed one). Assertions unchanged.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts`: the "prefers the metadata service definition" pin asserted that the engine is never probed for a seeded object. The S1b union probes it once per seeded object, for the roll-up strip alone, so the pin now asserts exactly that probe list. Its claim stands: the engine double registers no schema, so the resolved references prove the metadata definition was used.

Package installs go through the same loader:
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` applies a package's seeds with `new SeedLoaderService(...)`;
- so does `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts`;
- so do the single-tenant boot seed, the per-organization replay and the reseed paths in `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`.

The only seed path outside the loader is the runtime's basic-insert fallback (see above and the Acceptance notes).

No existing pin asserted that a seed load keeps a roll-up value. `engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts` "an isSystem create keeps its value" pins the engine's `isSystem` exemption, which this PR does not change.

## Tests

Pins. Each asserts the stored rows or the engine's calls, plus the warn notice. None reads a count key.

- `packages/objectql/src/seed-summary-never-stored.test.ts`, on the real ObjectQL engine and the real `SeedLoaderService`. The parent has a `sum`, a `count` and a `readonly` `max` roll-up, seeded with 999 / 99 / 500, over lines of 10 and 32.
  - Case 3: a parent alone stores 0 / 0 / empty, with one notice `{ object: 'ss_inv', fields: [line_total, line_count, line_max], droppedValues: 3 }`.
  - Case 1 (control): parent and children in one load store 42 / 2 / 32.
  - Case 4: a re-seed over existing children keeps 42 / 2 / 32 and is `skipped`, in `upsert` and in `update` mode.
  - Case 6: the same seed replayed stores 42 / 2 / 32 on both loads.
  - A roll-up an extension contributes (`registerObject(..., 'extend')`, engine-fallback rung) is dropped like the base object's own.
  - A seed with no roll-up value gives no notice.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-summary-stale.test.ts`, on the file's existing engine double:
  - `a seed never hands the engine a roll-up value`: no `insert` or `update` payload carries a roll-up key; a supplied `null` counts; a roll-up-only difference writes nothing; another change is written without the roll-up; `validate` gives the notice and writes nothing; a `currency` CONTROL is written as authored with no notice.
  - New this round (S1b), `a roll-up an object extension contributes is never seeded either`: the metadata double's copy lacks the extension's roll-up and the engine double's `getSchema` has it. Neither roll-up reaches the engine, and the one notice reads `{ object: 'ext_invoice', fields: ['paid', 'ext_refunds'], droppedValues: 2 }`. CONTROL: an engine whose `getSchema` throws leaves the metadata copy the only source; its roll-up is still dropped, and `ext_refunds` (declared a roll-up nowhere) is written as authored.

## Acceptance notes

- The runtime's basic-insert fallback seeder (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, the two `ql.insert` loops under "basic insert fallback") writes seed records with a plain `ql.insert`. It runs only when no metadata service is present (logged at debug) or the loader throws (logged at warn). Ruling D routes the change through the loader only, so on that path a roll-up value still reaches the engine. `fields.mdx` and the changeset now both say so.
- The loader does not rewrite rows that an earlier load stored a supplied total on. The next child write recomputes them; a parent with no child rows gets none, and `os migrate summary-nulls` backfills only `NULL` columns, so the changeset and the migration entry name the manual repair.
- A dataset keyed on a summary field (an `externalId` naming a roll-up) would now see that key blank, and the record would be refused as a blank-key record. No such seed exists in the tree, and a roll-up is not a natural key.
- The drop is counted before the record's fate is known: a record later refused or skipped as create-only still counts in the notice (review nit n2, not taken).
- The published data skill (`skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md:146-147`) gives the right instruction ("Never seed the roll-up"), but its reason ("stored as written") is now out of date. Follow-up #36122.

## Verification

Read first, in order of risk:
1. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`: the `summaryFields` union in `loadDataset` and the strip loop right after `const record = { ...(seedResult.value ...) }`. The strip must run before every read of the record.
2. `packages/objectql/src/seed-summary-never-stored.test.ts`: cases 3, 4 and 6.
3. `.changeset/35655-seed-summary-value-not-stored.md`: the FROM → TO, the row-counter sentence, the compatibility note and the manual repair.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/seed-loader-summary-stale.test.ts`. Expect `Tests 14 passed (14)`; the extension case's notice names `paid` and `ext_refunds`.
